reviews.one_line_contribution: Inside a name-swapping wrapper on ALFWorld it plants a per-kitchen procedure binding (which of two look-alike appliances actually heats/cools/cleans) and independently switches whether a wrong choice answers back ('Nothing happens') or silently consumes the step, to show that a 60-token run-time-probe rule substitutes for a retriever when the environment gives a signal, while a ~900-token observation-keyed table compiled from the same bank substitutes for it when the environment gives none.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Closest verified: MEMENTO, arXiv:2505.16348 ('Embodied Agents Meet Personalization: Investigating Challenges and Solutions Through the Lens of Memory Utilization', 2025-05-22, 12 cites; verified with `s2cli.py paper 2505.16348`, S2 channel). It plants exactly this proposal's independent variable — instance-specific bindings in an embodied household environment that are recoverable only from stored episodes (user-specific object semantics and routines) — and it already separates memory retrieval from memory application, which is the split this proposal advertises as new relative to Mem2ActBench. It does not threaten the core: it never scores a retriever against a compiled static artifact built from the same experience at matched tokens, and it never manipulates whether the binding can be probed before committing, which is this proposal's actual axis. Second threat, verified: SGR-Bench arXiv:2605.22219 (2026-05-21) — state-gated retrieval is precisely the 'testable' regime (state must be established, and the site tells you when it is wrong); it is a benchmark of failures, not a manipulation, and has no compiled-vs-retrieved arms. A third body of work the proposal never engages bounds two of its predictions rather than its headline: context-vs-parametric knowledge conflict (arXiv:2506.06485 'What Is Seen Cannot Be Unseen', returned by my --recent query on the HF channel; arXiv:2604.22193, 2026-04-24, same query). P1 ('does the reader keep its prior over a corrected exemplar?') and P3 ('will the reader prefer a retrieved trajectory's appliance name to its prior?') are context-memory conflict questions in agent clothing, and that literature already reports readers falling back on internal knowledge under conflict. That makes P1's and P3's mechanism less new than the proposal claims, though the testable/untestable interaction on top of it is not preempted.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline interaction is half stipulated, and the proposal says so itself: 'under untestable the rule is inert by construction', and D(S1, untestable) within +-8 of D(S0, untestable) is filed as a 'construction check, reported not scored'. So the 'only when untestable' claim decomposes into (a) a wrapper property the authors built, not a finding, and (b) three reader-capability facts about one 32B model — can it execute a two-branch probe rule, can it route a 30-row observation-keyed table to the right row, will it override 'microwave heats' when a retrieved trajectory says stoveburner. An AC will say: you constructed an environment in which a rule cannot possibly fire, then reported that the rule does not fire. Compounding this, the binding is not a generic instance-specific binding but a deliberate collision with the reader's parametric prior, and there is no binding level that avoids that collision (e.g. which of two identically-named cabinets is the working one), so every headline number is confounded with knowledge-conflict strength and may not survive a backbone change — a limitation the Risk section concedes but the design does not address. Finally the framing is inconsistent with its own P4: if the compiled table matches retrieval under untestable, the paper's result is 'you never need a retriever, compile a keyed table', which is the opposite of the title's 'A Query Is Needed Only for Untestable Bindings'; the hypothesis rescues this only by redefining 'per-instance lookup' to include a cached static table, which is exactly not a query.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Add a binding level that does not fight the parametric prior (two same-named receptacles, or an arbitrary tag, rather than microwave<->stoveburner), so P1/P3 measure binding transfer rather than knowledge-conflict strength; report the swap penalty at both levels. 2) Run the third regime the proposal excludes (undetectable but reversible) with the 30-token redundancy rule, so that the 'best static alternative' retrieval is scored against is measured rather than fixed by the wrapper's design; as written, the untestable wrapper is built to defeat every cheap static artifact except enumeration, which is what P4 then tests. 3) Fix P6: make W- carry the opposite binding deterministically instead of a random other-kitchen item that is correct about half the time under complementary assignments, which halves the estimand against a 12-point margin and biases the test toward falsification. 4) Define the 12-20 band for the P1 gate; as written, continuation is undefined in that band, and the entailment check is right that D(S0)-D(S3) collapses algebraically to a single swapped-game contrast. 5) Put the table's row count in the design (30 -> 100 -> 300 rows by merging kitchens or importing bindings) — the table-vs-query crossover lives exactly where the proposal declines to look, and P4 without it reads as an artifact of a benchmark with ~30 kitchens. 6) Retitle to what P4 actually claims. Dropping the type-agnostic T0/T1 or one seed pays for 1-3 within the same ~11.5 h budget.
reviews.missing_baseline: The redundancy static rule under untestable — a ~30-token 'do the procedure step at both candidate appliances' instruction on top of static3. The proposal names it and refuses it, on the grounds that the untestable wrapper makes later attempts on either appliance return the success string without effect. That is a wrapper decision, not a property of silent real-world failures (silent API/UI failures are frequently retry-safe), and it means the 'best static arm' that every retrieval residual is reported against is chosen by construction rather than measured, which is a direct violation of the brief's binding rule that retrieval be scored against the best static alternative built from the same experience. It is also far cheaper than the ~900-token table, so if it works the paper's cost story changes sign. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also ask for: a non-prior-conflicting binding level (see above), and a second backbone restricted to P2 and P4, since both are reader-capability operations rather than environment properties.

reviews.one_line_contribution: In ALFWorld, plant scene-specific procedure bindings (which of two identically-behaving appliances actually heats/cools/cleans) and cross that with whether a wrong choice is detectable before committing, to show that a per-instance lookup (scene-keyed retrieval, or an observation-keyed compiled table) is necessary only in the untestable regime, while in the testable regime a 60-token 'try it and switch' rule buys the same accuracy at zero uncached prefill.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The strongest threat I verified is LongMemEval-V2 (arXiv:2605.12493, 2026-05-12, verified via the literature command, S2+HF), which is built precisely around agents acquiring *environment-specific* experience and ships two memory methods that are the same contrast this proposal makes its headline: AgentRunbook-R, a RAG memory over raw state observations and strategy notes, versus AgentRunbook-C, which compiles trajectory-derived knowledge once, compared on accuracy *and* latency. That is retrieval-vs-compiled-artifact on instance-specific environment knowledge under a cost axis, i.e. the proposal's S2-vs-R3 comparison, already published four months ago and never cited here. It does not fully pre-empt: it does not plant the binding, does not manipulate whether the binding is probe-able at run time, and has no run-time-test rule arm, so the 'only when untestable' axis survives. Second, ScrambleToolBench (arXiv:2608.02358, 2026-08-03, verified, literature command) already benchmarks agents discovering hidden per-environment behaviors by interaction and reports they over-explore rather than use their own map, which is most of what P2 and P5 would find. Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv:2409.07429, verified) is the closest named compiled method and does not, as the proposal says, contain a probe or a bindings manipulation. Also verified: SGR-Bench 2605.22219, Mem2ActBench 2601.19935, SWE-ContextBench 2602.08316, 'When Agents Commit Too Soon' 2606.22936, ICAL 2406.14596, task-recognition-vs-task-learning 2305.09731, Preping 2605.13880 — all real and all described accurately. I did not individually verify the remaining IDs listed inside the proposal's own collision-check result lists (2609.04148, 2604.00356, 2512.01945, 2607.12397, 2501.01702, 2605.13511, 2506.04579, 2210.03821, 2608.10509, 2607.20999, 2603.21520, 2605.24117); several of them (2606.19911, 2608.07169, 2309.07900, 2202.12837) came back in my own searches and check out.
reviews.strongest_objection: The manipulated axis is not testability, it is testability confounded with irreversibility, and the proposal knowingly runs only the diagonal of the 2x2. 'Untestable' here means the wrong action returns a success string AND silently spends the procedure step AND cannot be undone; 'testable' means it returns 'Nothing happens' AND is free. Any interaction found is therefore equally explained by 'a query is needed when a mistake is unrecoverable' — a different and much older claim. The proposal names this in its limitations and then declines to run the third cell, which is exactly the cell that would identify the axis its title claims. Compounding this, the rule half of the headline interaction is definitional: the untestable regime is constructed so the probe rule can never receive its trigger, so D(S1, untestable) = D(S0, untestable) is an arithmetic consequence of the wrapper, not a result — which is precisely what Appendix B's 'no prediction entailed by a definition' rule forbids, and the automated entailment check flags the same thing. What is actually tested is the sufficiency half (can this reader use a retrieved name, or route a 30-row table), which is a Qwen3-32B competence measurement, not a law about when memory needs a query. A second, concrete objection: 'untestable' is untestable only against the one probe the experimenter chose. The wrapper hides the *procedure* response, but the receptacles' contents are explicitly not rewritten ('a fridge full of plates is a weak leak'), so `examine`/`open` remains a free, non-committing test of which appliance is which. That both contradicts the stated leak probe (which demands byte-identical strings for open/examine on both pair members) and means a reader with a slightly better rule — 'open both, act on the one that looks like a fridge' — would remove the penalty under 'untestable' with no memory at all, collapsing P3.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Run the 2x2 of {feedback signal present/absent} x {wrong attempt reversible/irreversible}, or at minimum add the undetectable-but-reversible cell that is currently cut; without it the title's causal variable is not identified. The cheap version: keep the untestable string but let the procedure step be retried, and add the 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' redundancy rule the proposal already describes as the answer there — if redundancy removes the penalty, the necessity claim is about irreversibility, not testability. (2) Resolve the leak contradiction: either rewrite receptacle contents so that no non-committing inspection distinguishes the pair (and re-run the leak probe on open/examine, reporting the strings), or drop the 'untestable' label and call the regime 'costly-to-test'. (3) Make P1's undefined 12-20 band a decision rule, and drop the TOST conjuncts in P2 and P4, which are implied by their companion '<= 12' claims plus the ~0 floor on D and so add no falsifiable content. (4) Fix P6: W-'s random other-kitchen item carries the correct binding half the time under q = .5, so W+ - W- estimates roughly half the locate-and-use effect against a 12-point margin; force W- to a kitchen with the opposite binding. (5) State the interaction as a pre-registered difference-in-differences with a power calculation, not as two separate '<= 12' bounds against a +-8 floor — a 12-point residual is a large effect to declare 'removed'.
reviews.missing_baseline: A no-memory inspection-probe arm under the untestable regime: a rule that uses free, non-committing actions (open/examine both appliances, or the redundancy rule 'do the step at both') rather than the procedure action itself. Under the plan as written, only the procedure action is silenced, so this arm can plausibly remove the swap penalty with zero retrieval and zero compiled binding — and if it does, P3's 'a per-instance lookup is necessary' is false as stated. A reviewer will ask for it because the proposal itself describes the redundancy rule and then declares its regime out of scope. Second omission: a retrieval placebo matched to W-, i.e. R3 with the three retrieved items forced to a kitchen carrying the opposite binding. R3o (oracle) bounds the retriever from above but nothing bounds it from below, so a positive R3 result cannot be attributed to the transferred binding rather than to generic same-type trajectory quality.

reviews.one_line_contribution: An ALFWorld text wrapper that plants per-kitchen appliance-name bindings (which of two identical-looking receptacles heats/cools/cleans) and crosses them with whether a wrong choice is detectable from feedback, to show that a per-instance lookup - scene-keyed retrieval or a reader-routed compiled table - beats a 60-token run-time-probe instruction only in the regime where the environment returns no signal.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The strongest verified threats are partial, not pre-emptive. 2606.22936 'When Agents Commit Too Soon' (verified via s2cli paper; S2 channel) already frames silent, unrecoverable commitment as the failure mode the untestable regime instantiates, but it is a hidden-state diagnostic and manipulates neither testability nor the memory form. 2605.22219 SGR-Bench (verified) already establishes that agents fail by not establishing the correct site-specific state, i.e. the 'binding' half of this proposal, without any static-vs-retrieved contrast. The sharpest threat to the *informativeness* of P1/P3 is 2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory' (returned by my recent-restricted mechanism search on the HF channel; I did not run a `paper` verification on it, so treat the ID as search-returned rather than individually verified), which already reports that readers adopt conflicting retrieved memory early and compound on it - i.e. that a retrieved name overrides a prior is closer to known than the proposal's P1/P3 framing admits. 2608.26730 'Knowing When Not to Reuse: Conditional Experience Transfer' (verified) is the nearest thing to the probe-before-reuse idea, but it authorizes reuse with bounded trials before *weight-changing training*, not at inference, so it does not pre-empt. None of these plants bindings, manipulates feedback testability, or runs rule/table/retrieval arms on the same games. The prior the proposal cannot search away is structural rather than bibliographic: 'you need stored information exactly for the latent state you cannot observe' is the textbook POMDP observability statement, and a skeptical AC will read the headline as an empirical restatement of it.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central 'only when untestable' interaction is manufactured by the wrapper rather than discovered, and the proposal's own P4 contradicts its title. Three parts. (a) The rule half of the interaction is definitional and the proposal says so: under untestable the probe rule 'is inert by construction', and D(S1, untestable) is filed as a construction check, not a prediction. What remains under testable is a compliance measurement - does a 32B reader execute a two-branch instruction when the environment tells it the branch fired - which is a fact about the reader, not about when experience memory needs a query. (b) P4 predicts that a compiled ~30-row table (a static, cached, once-compiled artifact) removes the untestable penalty as fully as retrieval does. If that holds, a query is *never* necessary in this study, in either regime; the surviving claim is 'a per-instance lookup is necessary', where 'lookup' includes a prompt, which is compile_dont_retrieve (archived 6.0) restated with a manipulation attached rather than overturned. The retrieval-vs-table distinction is then routing mechanism (reader-routed signature vs embedding-routed key), not memory necessity, and the title overclaims relative to what the plan can return. (c) Necessity is preserved only by excluding the obvious binding-free workaround: the proposal itself names a ~30-token redundancy rule ('do the step at both appliances') that would remove the untestable penalty with no memory at all, and rules it out by making the untestable regime irreversible by authorial choice - the failed step is silently spent, later attempts are no-ops. Irreversibility is a property of the wrapper, not of ALFWorld or of real silent-API settings, so the 'query is necessary' half is engineered. Secondary but concrete: the manipulation is a lexical-prior fight (calling a stoveburner 'microwave'), so P1/P3 measure knowledge-conflict override under adversarial renaming rather than acquisition of an arbitrary instance binding, and the result will not transfer to bindings the model has no prior about. And the untestable regime's leak probe covers only non-procedure actions across swap states; it does not verify that post-procedure state inspection (examine the object after the fake success string) fails to reveal the silent failure - if it does reveal it, the untestable regime is probe-able after all and P3 measures something else.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Drop the 'query' framing the plan cannot support and pre-register the honest headline: which *artifact* form carries an unobservable instance binding - reader-routed table vs scene-keyed retrieval vs oracle - with the query-necessity claim retired unless S2 fails. (2) Run the redundancy rule as a first-class arm under untestable (the 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' instruction), and add the third regime the proposal excludes (undetectable but reversible). If a binding-free redundancy rule matches retrieval, that is the paper's real and more interesting result; suppressing the arm makes the necessity claim unfalsifiable. (3) Add a neutral-name binding level (appliance_a / appliance_b, or novel tokens) alongside the microwave/stoveburner swap, so prior-override and binding-acquisition are separated; report the interaction of binding lexicality with regime. Without it a reviewer reads the whole study as a knowledge-conflict experiment. (4) Fix the statistics the entailment check already flagged: delete the TOST conjuncts in P2 and P4 (each is implied by its own first conjunct plus the near-zero floor on D, which violates the brief's no-prediction-entailed-by-a-definition rule), define the 12-20 band left open in P1, re-specify W- so it carries a known-wrong binding rather than the correct one half the time, and extend the leak probe to post-procedure state inspection under untestable.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. Primary: the binding-free redundancy rule under untestable - a ~30-token 'perform the procedure step at both candidate appliances' instruction on the static3 base. The proposal names it and excludes it by declaring the untestable regime irreversible; a reviewer will demand it, because it is the cheapest artifact that could remove the untestable penalty with no bank, no table and no query, and its success would falsify the headline without touching any of P1-P6. Secondary: k0 (no-memory) at q = .5 under both regimes. It is cut on the assertion that 'a stale prior is the same floor as a stale exemplar', but S0's exemplars actively name the wrong appliance, so the swap penalty of a memory-free reader is the correct reference for deciding whether the penalty is caused by the stale artifact or by the model's lexical prior - exactly the attribution the paper needs for P1 and P3.
